extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, authors, peer reviewers, journal editors, and policymakers preparing or assessing health economic evaluations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for reporting economic evaluations of health interventions (the consolidated CHEERS 2022 statement), intended to help authors produce complete, transparent reports and help reviewers/editors assess reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS 2022 checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) Statement: Updated Reporting Guidance for Health Economic Evaluations. Reporting guideline provided for: Economic evaluations of health interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CHEERS 2022 checklist (PDF) and an interactive checklist are provided to generate a completed Word or PDF checklist. The guideline was published simultaneously in multiple journals (bibliographic references listed). The checklist is intended to improve the reporting completeness and transparency of economic evaluations and applies to the whole report. See the full bibliographic reference (Husereau et al., CHEERS 2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — study design applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Study design: Economic evaluations. Applies to the whole report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHEERS 2022 is targeted specifically at economic evaluations of health interventions rather than other study types; authors should use the checklist to cover reporting across the entire manuscript (not just individual sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation and Elaboration document
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards (CHEERS) 2022 Explanation and Elaboration: a report that expands on the checklist items and provides detailed guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Explanation and Elaboration paper (Husereau et al., Value Health. 2022;25(1):10-31) accompanies the checklist and provides extended guidance, examples, and clarifications for how to apply each checklist item. Users should consult this document when completing or assessing CHEERS items.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS-VOI (Value of Information) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: CHEERS Value of Information (CHEERS-VOI) Reporting Standards - Explanation and Elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specialised extension exists for Value of Information analyses (reference provided: Kunst et al., Value Health. 2023). Use the VOI extension when the economic evaluation includes formal value-of-information methods; follow the extension's additional reporting expectations alongside the main CHEERS checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS-AI extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards for Interventions that use Artificial Intelligence (CHEERS-AI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specialised extension (CHEERS-AI) addresses reporting expectations for evaluations of interventions that use artificial intelligence; when applicable, authors should follow CHEERS-AI in addition to the main CHEERS 2022 checklist (reference provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and patient involvement recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation for greater public involvement in health economic evaluation reporting, including a guide for patient representatives and organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commentary advocating for greater public involvement is noted; supplementary materials include a guide for patient representatives and organisations developed following suggestions from the CHEERS 2022 Public Reference Group. Authors and guideline users should consider patient/public involvement principles and available guidance when designing, reporting, or appraising evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability in additional languages / translations
rubrics_metrics.description: CHEERS 2022 and prior CHEERS translations are available in multiple languages (Spanish, Turkish, French, Chinese, Japanese, Dutch, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translated/adapted versions of the checklist and accompanying materials exist for several languages and jurisdictions (references listed). Use country/language-appropriate translations where available to support local authors, reviewers, and stakeholders.
